html:
The Sicilian Expedition was a huge Athenian attack on Syracuse in Sicily from 415 to 413 BCE, during the Peloponnesian War. It ended in one of the worst defeats in Greek history.

A small Sicilian city asked Athens for help against its neighbour. Alcibiades argued for a great campaign; Nicias argued against it and, trying to put the Assembly off, said it would need a vast force. The Assembly voted for one. Just before the fleet sailed, the herms were smashed and Alcibiades was accused. He was recalled soon after landing and fled to Sparta.

At Syracuse the Athenians began to wall the city in. Then the Spartan general Gylippus arrived and turned the tide. A second Athenian fleet under Demosthenes could not save things. An eclipse of the moon in August 413 BCE delayed the retreat, the Athenian fleet was destroyed in the harbour, and the army was cut down as it tried to escape overland. Nicias and Demosthenes were executed, and thousands of prisoners were left to die in the stone quarries of Syracuse.

Athens lost much of its fleet and money. Within two years came the oligarchic coup.
